ceiling_label: CEILING: every metric here is an IN-SAMPLE CEILING on the same history the periods were fit on. The oracle buys the whole book all-in on every pinned buy date and sells all-out on every pinned sell date, so it measures PERIOD QUALITY, never achievable performance — real DCA drips and cannot buy one close. Only the split-sample read (fit on the first half, score on the unseen second half) says anything out-of-sample-ish, and both sides must be read next to this sentence. The long-first rebuild changes WHICH periods are chosen, not what the number means: selecting on prominence and capping covered days is still selection on the same history, so pure-long and every graded rung are the same kind of ceiling.
objective_label: frozen objective: maximize oracle Sharpe, tie-break Calmar, then CAGR, subject to a time-in-market floor of 70.0% of days (period_optimize.EXPOSURE_FLOOR_PCT / rank_period_scores)
risk_conventions_label: risk-adjusted conventions (sdca/risk_metrics.py): simple per-day returns, annualization 252, risk-free 0, drawdown reused from walk_forward.
model_label: long-first period model (Plan 21): the LONG secular set is selected FIRST as the primary regime — prominence-ranked pivots under a 25.0% peak-day cap at the frozen default half-width — then MEDIUM windows are added ONE RUNG AT A TIME (shorter window first, earlier date breaking ties). A rung is kept only when it is HIT (caught a real move), strictly improves oracle Sharpe, and clears the frozen 70.0% floor; the first failure stops the ladder. The floor is NEVER relaxed, and peak/trough day shares are SEPARATE quantities — only peak days bound the floor.
holdout_note: in-sample by construction: this run scores the FULL cached GLD history, the same history the periods are derived from. No separate holdout segment was carved out or touched; the split-sample pair below is the only out-of-sample-ish read.
floor_note: the time-in-market floor is NEVER relaxed in this run

long_selection.half_width_note: frozen default half-width (min of the long grid), passed as None so the default is what runs; this task does not sweep widths
long_selection.day_share_note: peak and trough day shares are SEPARATE (the cap is applied per kind); only peak days are the flat time that bounds the exposure floor

calendar_bound_pins.rule: a selected pin is calendar-bound when pin +/- half_width_days falls beyond either calendar edge (first bar or last bar); derived here from LongTermSelection.half_width_days because the model does not carry it

split_sample.note: the long-first fit half selects its own long set and grades its own medium ladder, then the windows it kept are scored on the unseen half; a window falling before the split does not act there (the oracle ignores out-of-calendar pins)
split_sample.defect_note: the out-of-sample side of a split-sample is structurally binary — a filed 1-bit defect: a fitted window straddling the split collapses its enter onto the first unseen bar, so the book is either all-in at the split or flat forever. Both sides are printed anyway (the fit half's own ladder, and the unseen-half score of the windows it kept) so the out-of-sample read is visible rather than null.
